_meta.semantics: covers_syllabus_refs is an index of the objectives a stage is principally associated with; coverage is claimed only through _syllabus_items + covers_items, and only as far as coverage_check.py confirms.

_items_source.document: AQA AS and A-level Chemistry (7404/7405) specification: subject content 3.1-3.3, mathematical requirements (section 6) and practical assessment (section 8)
_items_source.version: Version 1.2 (July 2026), linked from aqa.org.uk/7405 and itemised 2026-09-27
_items_source.numbering: AQA's own codes: content at the deepest numbered level (3.1.1.1-3.3.16), mathematical skills MS 0.0-MS 4.3, practical skills PS1.1-PS4.1, apparatus and techniques ATa-ATl, and the twelve required practicals numbered RP1-RP12 in AQA's order.

_syllabus_items.title: Relative atomic mass and relative molecular mass
The mole and the Avogadro constant
Nature of covalent and dative covalent bonds
Shapes of simple molecules and ions
Effect of temperature on reaction rate
Chemical equilibria and Le Chatelier's principle
Equilibrium constant Kc for homogeneous systems
Gibbs free-energy change, ∆G, and entropy change, ∆S (A-level only)
Equilibrium constant Kp for homogeneous systems (A-level only)
Commercial applications of electrochemical cells (A-level only)
Brønsted–Lowry acid–base equilibria in aqueous solution (A-level only)
Definition and determination of pH (A-level only)
The ionic product of water, Kw (A-level only)
Weak acids and bases Ka for weak acids (A-level only)
pH curves, titrations and indicators (A-level only)
Properties of Period 3 elements and their oxides (A-level only)
General properties of transition metals (A-level only)
Reactions of ions in aqueous solution (A-level only)
Identification of functional groups by test-tube reactions
Biodegradability and disposal of polymers (A-level only)
Recognise and make use of appropriate units in calculation
Recognise and use expressions in decimal and ordinary form
Use calculators to find and use power, exponential and logarithmic functions
Use an appropriate number of significant figures
Identify uncertainties in measurements and use simple techniques to determine uncertainty when data are combined
Understand and use the symbols =, <, <<, >>, >, ∝, ~ and the equilibrium sign
Change the subject of an equation
Substitute numerical values into algebraic equations using appropriate units for physical quantities
Use logarithms in relation to quantities that range over several orders of magnitude
Translate information between graphical, numerical and algebraic forms
Plot two variables from experimental or other data
Determine the slope and intercept of a linear graph
Calculate rate of change from a graph showing a linear relationship
Draw and use the slope of a tangent to a curve as a measure of rate of change
Use angles and shapes in regular 2D and 3D structures
Visualise and represent 2D and 3D forms, including two-dimensional representations of 3D objects
Understand the symmetry of 2D and 3D shapes
Solve problems set in practical contexts

_syllabus_items.title: Required practical 1: make up a volumetric solution and carry out a simple acid-base titration
Required practical 2: measurement of an enthalpy change
Required practical 3: investigation of how the rate of a reaction changes with temperature
Required practical 4: test-tube reactions to identify Group 2 cations and NH4+, and halide, OH-, CO3 2- and SO4 2- anions
Required practical 5: distillation of a product from a reaction
Required practical 6: tests for alcohol, aldehyde, alkene and carboxylic acid
Required practical 7: measuring the rate of reaction by an initial rate method and by a continuous monitoring method
Required practical 8: measuring the EMF of an electrochemical cell
Required practical 9: pH changes when a weak acid reacts with a strong base and a strong acid with a weak base
Required practical 10: preparation of a pure organic solid (with a purity test) and a pure organic liquid
Required practical 11: test-tube reactions to identify transition metal ions in aqueous solution
Required practical 12: separation of species by thin-layer chromatography
